title: The Painting with an Uncertain Blue
title_ja: 不確かな青を持つ絵画
fact_notes: 架空の教材例・思考実験。実在の調査、統計、制度、実証結果ではない。登録台帳は制作来歴確認用。

sentences.en: A fictional art museum receives a damaged painting whose background has lost much of its original color.
sentences.ja: 架空の美術館は背景の元の色が多く失われた損傷絵画を受け取る。

sentences.en: The conservator examines the remaining surface and discovers several small areas containing traces of blue pigment.
sentences.ja: 修復専門家は残った表面を調べ青の顔料の痕跡がある小部分を見つける。

sentences.en: A visitor who sees a photograph of the painting suggests restoring the entire background to a bright blue.
sentences.ja: 絵画の写真を見た来館者は背景すべてを鮮やかな青へ修復することを提案する。

sentences.en: The conservator explains that evidence of a color in one section does not necessarily establish its appearance throughout the original painting.
sentences.ja: 一部分の色の証拠は元の絵全体の外観を必ずしも確定しないと説明する。

sentences.en: The museum considers several possible ways of presenting the artwork.
sentences.ja: 美術館は作品提示のいくつかの方法を検討する。

sentences.en: A fully restored image might be easier for visitors to understand, but it could also create the impression that uncertain details had been independently verified.
sentences.ja: 全面修復画像は理解しやすいかもしれないが不確かな詳細が独立確認された印象を作り得る。

sentences.en: Leaving every damaged area untouched would preserve the visible evidence, although some visitors might find the composition difficult to recognize.
sentences.ja: 損傷部を全てそのまま残せば目に見える証拠を保存できるが構図を認識しにくい観客もいるかもしれない。

sentences.en: The museum therefore distinguishes the physical preservation of the object from the creation of an interpretive reconstruction.
sentences.ja: そこで物理的保存と解釈的復元の作成を区別する。

sentences.en: The conservator prepares digital illustrations showing several plausible versions of the missing background.
sentences.ja: 修復専門家は失われた背景の複数の妥当な復元案を示すデジタル図を作る。

sentences.en: Each illustration is accompanied by a description of the evidence used and the assumptions required to complete it.
sentences.ja: 各図には利用根拠と完成に必要な前提の説明が添えられる。

sentences.en: Visitors can compare the interpretations without mistaking any one of them for a photograph of the original work.
sentences.ja: 来館者はどれかを原画の写真と誤解せず解釈を比較できる。

sentences.en: The museum also explains that these visualizations are educational examples rather than instructions for the treatment of an actual historical painting.
sentences.ja: これらは実在歴史絵画の処置指示でなく教材例だとも説明する。

sentences.en: During an imaginary exhibition, one visitor expresses disappointment that the original background cannot be recovered with certainty.
sentences.ja: 架空展示で一来館者は元の背景が確実に復元できないことへの失望を表す。

sentences.en: Another finds the competing versions interesting because they reveal how a small piece of evidence can support several different possibilities.
sentences.ja: 別の来館者は小さな根拠が複数の可能性を支え得ることを示す競合案を興味深く感じる。

sentences.en: The conservator acknowledges that uncertainty can be difficult to communicate when an image appears complete and visually convincing.
sentences.ja: 画像が完成し視覚的に説得的に見えると不確実性を伝えにくいと認める。

sentences.en: The labels therefore identify speculative elements even when those elements look perfectly natural within an illustration.
sentences.ja: そこでラベルは図中で完全に自然に見える推測要素も特定する。

sentences.en: An artistic reconstruction can help people imagine a lost appearance without providing decisive evidence that the appearance is historically accurate.
sentences.ja: 芸術的復元は歴史的正確さの決定的根拠を示さず失われた外観を想像する助けになり得る。

sentences.en: The challenge is to make an interpretation accessible without allowing its visual completeness to conceal its limitations.
sentences.ja: 課題は視覚的完成度で限界を隠さず解釈を理解しやすくすることだ。

sentences.en: A museum can encourage appreciation of a damaged artwork while helping its audience recognize the distinction between what survives and what is imagined.
sentences.ja: 美術館は残ったものと想像したものの区別を観客に認識させつつ損傷芸術品の鑑賞を促せる。

sentences.en: In this case, the uncertain blue becomes a reminder that responsible reconstruction requires judgment as well as imagination.
sentences.ja: この場合不確かな青は責任ある復元に想像力と判断が必要であることを思い出させる。

vocabulary.definition: in a way that must occur
feeling when hopes are not met

questions.prompt: What remains on the painting's surface?
Why is restoring all of the background to bright blue uncertain?
options: Evidence from one section does not establish the entire original appearance.
The visitor has already proven the color.

questions.prompt: What risk comes with a complete-looking restored image?
options: It guarantees that no visitor understands the work.
It may make uncertain details appear verified.
It makes all evidence disappear immediately.
It proves the original artist used no color.
questions.explanation_ja: 確実そうに見えるリスク。

options: Evidence and assumptions used to create it.
A claim that it is the original photograph.
An instruction for treating real historical art.
To assert all versions are historically correct.
To make the background impossible to see.

questions.prompt: How did one visitor respond to uncertainty?
options: They claimed all versions were identical.
They were disappointed the original could not be recovered with certainty.
They refused to see any image.
questions.explanation_ja: 確実な復元ができない失望。

questions.prompt: Why identify speculative elements in labels?
options: All elements have been independently verified.
Labels are meant to hide the evidence.
questions.explanation_ja: 視覚的自然さと確実性は別。

options: Reconstruction can inspire imagination while clearly distinguishing evidence from speculation.
Digital images prove the original appearance.

grammar.focus: without mistaking any one of them

paraphrases.rewrite: Leaving damage unchanged preserves evidence but may make the composition harder to recognize.

paraphrases.source: Visitors can compare the interpretations without mistaking any one of them for a photograph of the original work.
